rewrites.//: SPA catch-all — but it must NOT swallow requests for build artefacts. Before this exclusion, a request for a chunk that no longer exists (any tab or PWA shell still running a previous build after a deploy) fell through to this rule and got index.html back with HTTP 200 and Content-Type: text/html. The browser was asking for a module script, so it rejected the response with "'text/html' is not a valid JavaScript MIME type" (Safari) / "Expected a JavaScript module script..." (Chrome) instead of a plain 404 — an error shape the client-side chunk-reload recovery did not recognise, so book pages dead-ended on the error screen. Excluding assets/, api/ and the service-worker files makes a missing chunk return a real 404, which surfaces as the recoverable "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module".

headers.//: Everything under /assets is content-hashed by Vite, so the filename changes whenever the bytes change. Serving it with max-age=0, must-revalidate (the default) made every visitor re-validate every chunk on every load for no benefit.
The shell and the service worker must never be cached — they are how a client discovers the current chunk hashes.
